children.text: Along with the actual caption at the bottom of the screen, “You know what no worries”, Connor also added a second caption to the top of the video. It’s different from the one he put in the bottom caption but still cohesive, both being humorous and casual. Adding a caption to the top of the video in pretty big text, gives the viewer an idea of the overall feel of the video right from the start. It sets the tone for the remainder of the post. It’s also very eye-catching. You naturally read that caption before reading the much smaller caption at the bottom. With such short attention spans in audiences now, it’s important to hook them and keep them hooked on your posts. Utilizing a much larger, more captivating caption at the top of the video grabs viewers’ attention, sets the tone for the video, and gains more traction overall.

TikTok has a really convenient feature where the creator can add closed captions to their videos to make the video even easier to follow. In doing this, it allows viewers to enjoy the video even if they’re unable to watch with audio. Expanding their audience to those who otherwise wouldn't have been able to enjoy the video to its fullest extent. For this video in particular, his audience is expanded in other ways as well. Not only does it attract his usual, younger audience and the deaf community, but it’s also bringing in fans of the show he’s currently on called Dancing with the Stars. It updates in real time with the speed of the audio as well, just like a television show, further adding to the convenience. Additionally, there’s not too much actively going on in the video to watch necessarily, so the closed captions add another level of visual appeal and keep the viewer engaged.

Connor Wood is a contestant on the newest season of Dancing with the Stars and they’ve been in full on rehearsal mode. The season premiere was September 15, 2026 but the preparation has been going on for months now. With talk show appearances and photoshoots and dance rehearsals, he’s been all in with this show. This is a clip of Connor and his dance partner Riley from a dance rehearsal for the premiere. In it, he messes up but then the humor continues as he proceeds to make the interaction even more awkward. It’s a great depiction of how authentic and funny all of Connor’s content is.

This video shows Connor completely misreading body language and signals. After messing up the choreography they were rehearsing, they shared some laughs and a couple of high fives before going back to practicing. As Rylee got into position to keep dancing, Connor mistook it as her holding her arms out for a hug. A funny, raw moment caught on camera. In all of Connor’s content, tiktok and podcast episodes, his main goal at the end of the day is to bring a smile to his audience's face and make others laugh. The reason behind posting this specific clip wasn’t to showcase his dancing for the show coming up or to brag about being on Dancing with the Stars. It was to show a genuine, embarrassing moment in order to make others laugh the way it made Connor and Riley laugh. It’s also a relatable circumstance. We all find ourselves in embarrassing moments, as much as we try not to. This video highlights how we are all similar and no one is perfect, and there’s beauty and humor in that.
